questions.question: Who among the following has served as the Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission of India?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following has served as the Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Pranab Mukherjee.

Key Points

  • Pranab Mukherjee
    • He was an Indian politician and has served as the 13th President of India, from 2012 to 2017.
    • A veteran in Indian politics, he has the rare distinction of having served as Foreign, Defence, Commerce, and Finance Minister at different times over his long and illustrious political career spanning several decades. In 1997, Pranab Mukherjee was voted an Outstanding Parliamentarian.
    • Active in West Bengal politics, he was the president of the state's unit of Congress since 1985 but resigned in July 2010.
    • Well-respected by politicians of all parties, Pranab Mukherjee is the Congress party's main troubleshooter and has often been called upon to guide the party through difficult situations.
    • He is married to Suvra Mukherjee and has two sons and one daughter.
    • In 2008, he was honoured with the Padma Vibhushan, the second-highest civilian award in India.
    • He became Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission from 1991 to 1996. Hence, Option 1 is correct.
    • He was awarded India's highest civilian honour, the Bharat Ratna, in 2019, by his successor as president, Ram Nath Kovind.

Additional Information

  • Ramaswamy Venkataraman
    • He was an Indian lawyer, Indian independence activist, and politician who served as a Union Minister and as the eighth president of India.
    • He was born in Rajamadam village in Tanjore district, Madras Presidency.
  • Pratibha Devisingh Patil
    • She is an Indian politician and lawyer who served as the 12th president of India from 25 July 2007 to July 2012 and was also the first and, to date, only female president of India. She is a member of the Indian National Congress.
  • Giani Zail Singh
    • He was the seventh and the first Sikh president of India serving from 1982 to 1987.
    • Prior to his presidency, he was a politician with the Indian National Congress Party and had held several ministerial posts in the Union Cabinet, including that of the Home Minister.

questions.question: Who among the following was a saint from Maharashtra?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following was a saint from Maharashtra?
questions.solution: Chokhamela was a saint from Maharashtra and is considered one of the earliest Dalit poets and social reformers in Indian history. He belonged to the Varkari movement, which emphasized devotion to Lord Vitthal and equality among all individuals, irrespective of caste or social status. Chokhamela’s poetry reflected his deep spirituality and his personal experiences of discrimination due to his caste. Despite facing societal challenges, he remained devoted to his faith and contributed significantly to the Bhakti tradition. His works continue to inspire generations in the pursuit of equality and devotion.

questions.question: In 1674, who used a single-lens microscope to examine pond water and observed dozens of protists, which he called 'animalcules', as well as spirogyra, or green algae?
questions.questionHtml: In 1674, who used a single-lens microscope to examine pond water and observed dozens of protists, which he called 'animalcules', as well as spirogyra, or green algae?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Anton Van Leeuwenhoek.

Key Points

  • Anton Van Leeuwenhoek is universally acknowledged as the father of microbiology.
  • He discovered both protists and bacteria.
  • In 1674 he likely observed protozoa for the first time and several years later bacteria.
  • Those “very little animalcules” he was able to isolate from different sources, such as rainwater, pond, well water, and the human mouth and intestine. He also calculated their sizes.

Additional Information

  • Robert Brown FRSE FRS FLS MWS was a Scottish botanist and paleobotanist who made important contributions to botany largely through his pioneering use of the microscope. 
  • Robert Hooke FRS was an English polymath active as a scientist and architect, who, using a microscope, was the first to visualize a micro-organism.
  • Rudolf Ludwig Carl Virchow was a German physician, anthropologist, pathologist, prehistorian, biologist, writer, editor, and politician.
  • He is known as "the father of modern pathology" and as the founder of social medicine, and to his colleagues, the "Pope of medicine".

questions.question: For which film did Asha Bhosle win the International Indian Film Academy (IIFA) Award in the Best Playback Singer Female category in 2002?
questions.questionHtml: For which film did Asha Bhosle win the International Indian Film Academy (IIFA) Award in the Best Playback Singer Female category in 2002?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Lagaan.

Key Points

  • Lagaan is a 2001 Indian epic sports-drama film directed by Ashutosh Gowariker.
  • The film features Aamir Khan in the lead role, who also produced the film.
  • Asha Bhosle won the International Indian Film Academy (IIFA) Award for Best Playback Singer Female in 2002 for the song "Radha Kaise Na Jale" from this film.
  • The song "Radha Kaise Na Jale" is a duet featuring Udit Narayan and Asha Bhosle, with music composed by A.R. Rahman and lyrics by Javed Akhtar.

Additional Information

  • International Indian Film Academy Awards (IIFA)
    • Established in 2000, the IIFA Awards are presented annually by the International Indian Film Academy to honor artistic and technical excellence in Bollywood.
    • The awards are held at a different international location each year, aiming to promote Indian cinema globally.
  • Asha Bhosle
    • Asha Bhosle is one of the most renowned and versatile playback singers in India, known for her voice's range and versatility.
    • She has recorded thousands of songs in multiple languages and is a recipient of numerous awards, including the Dadasaheb Phalke Award and the Padma Vibhushan.
  • A.R. Rahman
    • A.R. Rahman is an internationally acclaimed Indian composer, singer, and music producer, known for integrating Indian classical music with electronic music, world music, and traditional orchestral arrangements.
    • He has won multiple awards, including two Academy Awards, two Grammy Awards, a BAFTA Award, and a Golden Globe.
  • Lagaan
    • The film is set in 1893 during the late Victorian period of India's colonial British Raj.
    • Lagaan tells the story of the inhabitants of a small village, who, oppressed by high taxes, find themselves in an extraordinary situation as an arrogant British army officer challenges them to a game of cricket as a wager to avoid paying the taxes they owe.
    • The film was critically acclaimed and became the third Indian film to be nominated for the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film.

questions.question: In which year did the Tibetan Spiritual leader the Dalai Lama seek political asylum in India?
questions.questionHtml: In which year did the Tibetan Spiritual leader the Dalai Lama seek political asylum in India?
questions.solution:
In 1959, The Tibetan Spiritual leader the Dalai Lama seek political asylum in India.

  • The Dalai Lama fought his way through the snow on 31 March 1959 to reach Chutangmu, a tiny Assam Rifles outpost near Tawang, to apply for asylum in India. 
  • Dalai Lamas are important Gelug school monks, Tibetan Buddhism's newest school which was formally led by the Ganden Tripas.
  • The Dalai Lama has called on the rights of Tibetans to the United Nations. This appeal resulted in three resolutions adopted by the General Assembly in 1959, 1961 and 1965, all before being allowed to represent the People's Republic at the United Nations.
  • The Tibetan Institute of Performing Arts was founded in 1959, and in 1967 the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies became India's primary university for Tibetans.

questions.question: Who among the following was given the title of Mallika-e-Ghazal?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following was given the title of Mallika-e-Ghazal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Begum Akhtar.

  • Akhtari Bai Faizabadi, also known as Begum Akhtar, was an Indian singer and actress who was given the title of "Mallika-e-Ghazal" (Queen of Ghazals).

Key Points

  • The legendary Begum Akhtar was a doyen of Hindustani classical music, particularly in the ghazal genre.
  • Her musical tradition was so unique that she came to be associated with her own distinct style of singing. She was rightly called the ‘Mallika-e-Ghazal’.
  • She came to be associated with Hindustani classical music, excelling in ghazal, Dadra, and thumri.
  • As a child, Begum Akhtar or Akhtari Bai Faizabadi, began her classical music training rather early as she reportedly showed sparks even as a kid, captivated by the music of Chandra Bai, a touring theatre artist of the day. 
  • She received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for vocal music and was awarded Padma Shri and Padma Bhushan (posthumously) by Govt. of India.

Additional Information

  • Iqbal Bano was a ghazal singer from Pakistan. She was known for her semi-classical Urdu ghazal songs and classical thumris but also sang easy-listening numbers in 1950s films.
  • Nayyara Noor is a Pakistani playback singer who is considered one of the Indian subcontinent's popular film songs playback singers and a stage performer. She performs in live ghazal singing concerts on Pakistan television shows or in concert halls in the country.
  • Farida Khanum is a Pakistani classical singer from the city of Kolkata West Bengal. She is also known for her honorific title Malika-e-Ghazal in both Pakistan and India.

questions.question: Who among the following is called the ‘Bhajan Samrat’ of India?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following is called the ‘Bhajan Samrat’ of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Anup Jalota.

Key Points

  • Anup Jalota is renowned as the 'Bhajan Samrat' of India for his exceptional contribution to devotional music.
  • He has been awarded the Padma Shri, India's fourth highest civilian award, in 2012 for his contributions to the field of Art-Indian Classical Music - Vocal.

  • Bhajan:
    • A bhajan is a type of devotional song in Indian religions, typically expressing love and devotion to a deity.
    • Bhajans are often simple and lyrical, and they can be performed solo or in a group.
  • Ghazal:
    • A ghazal is a form of amatory poem or ode, originating in Arabic poetry, and is often sung in the Indian subcontinent.
    • Ghazals are typically centered around themes of love, loss, and longing.
  • Padma Shri:
    • Padma Shri is the fourth highest civilian award in the Republic of India.
    • It is awarded to citizens of India in recognition of their distinguished contribution in various spheres such as Arts, Education, Industry, Literature, Science, Sports, Medicine, Social Service and Public Affairs.
  • Indian Classical Music:
    • Indian classical music is categorized into two major traditions: Hindustani (North Indian) and Carnatic (South Indian).
    • It is characterized by its raga (melodic framework) and tala (rhythmic patterns).

questions.question: Kishori Amonkar is famous for which of the following forms of music?
questions.questionHtml: Kishori Amonkar is famous for which of the following forms of music?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Hindustani classical vocals.

Key Points

  • Kishori Amonkar
    • Leading Hindustani classical vocalist Kishori Amonkar (10 April 1932 – 3 April 2017) belonged to the Jaipur Gharana, or a group of performers who share a certain musical aesthetic.
    • She performed in the light classical genres of thumri and bhajan as well as the classical genre of khyal.
    • Amonkar studied under her mother Mogubai Kurdikar, a classical singer from the Jaipur Gharana, but throughout her career, she experimented with a range of vocal genres.
    • In 1987 and 2002, respectively, Amonkar was given the Padma Bhushan and the Padma Vibhushan, two of India's highest civilian honours.
    • She received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship in 2009 and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 1985.

Additional Information

  • Young Amonkar started taking vocal lessons in Hindustani classical music from Anjanibai Malpekar of the Bhendibazaar Gharana in the early 1940s.
  • She wrote about musical theory and practice in the Marathi book Swaraartha Ramani, which was published in 2010.
  • The documentary Bhinna Shadja, which was made by Amol Palekar and Sandhya Gokhale, features Amonkar as its subject.
  • In 1991, she also received the esteemed Dr T. M. A. Pai Outstanding Konkani Award and she was one of the seven recipients of the  M.S. Subbulakshmi Awards for classical music in 2016.

questions.question: India's first women's organisation, Bharat Stree Mahamandal, was founded by __________.
questions.questionHtml: <font style="vertical-align: inherit;"><font style="vertical-align: inherit;">India's first women's organisation, Bharat Stree Mahamandal, was founded by __________.</font></font>

options.html: <font style="vertical-align: inherit;"><font style="vertical-align: inherit;">Sarla Devi Chaudharani</font></font>

questions.solution:
The correct answer isSarala Devi ChaudhuraniKey Points

  • Bharat Stree Mahamandal (the Large Circle of Indian Women) was the first all India women’s association.
  • It was set up in 1910 by Sarala Devi Chaudhurani.
  • The centre was formed in Lahore in November 1910 at a personal meeting of women.
  • It was decided to hold the opening meeting in Allahabad in December 1910 when many from different parts of India were expected to assemble there for the Congress session.
  • The most important feature of the inaugural session of the Bharat Stree Mahamandal:
    • it was presided over by Her Highness the Begum Sahiba of Janjira, a Muslim woman, and
    • was graced by the presence of Her Highness the Nawab Begum of Bhopal, the only ruling princes of India and a Muslim woman as well.

Additional Information

  • The objective of Bharat Stree Mahamandal was the creation of an organization by means of which women of every race, creed, class and party in India may be brought together on the basis of their common interest in the moral and material progress of women in India; and in and through which organization they may work in association and in a spirit of mutual helpfulness for the progress of humanity that through her sex.

questions.question: Who showed that heating silver cyanide (an inorganic compound) with ammonium chloride (another inorganic compound) produced urea without the aid of any living organism or part of a living organism, in 1828?
questions.questionHtml: Who showed that heating silver cyanide (an inorganic compound) with ammonium chloride (another inorganic compound) produced urea without the aid of any living organism or part of a living organism, in 1828?
questions.solution:
Correct answer is Friedrich Wohler.

Key Points

  • Friedrich Wöhler was the first to synthesize an organic compound from an inorganic substance.
  • In 1828, he synthesized urea by slowly evaporating a water solution of ammonium cyanate, which he had prepared by adding silver cyanate to ammonium chloride.
  •  It is often cited as the starting point of modern organic chemistry.
  • Wöhler, Friedrich (1800–82) German chemist who first isolated aluminium and beryllium, and discovered calcium carbide.

Additional Information

  • Antoine Lavoisier​ is most noted for his discovery of the role oxygen plays in combustion Antoine Lavoisier was a French Chemist who discovered that air is responsible for combustion and the source of acidity.
  • Ernest Orlando Lawrence was a pioneering American nuclear physicist and winner of the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1939 for his invention of the cyclotron.
  • Alfred Werner was a Swiss chemist who was a student at ETH Zurich and a professor at the University of Zurich.
